Received my Tex Yoda a week ago and wanted to give my review after using over the last week. Like many buyers I've been a longtime fan of using the trackpoint since around 2001 when I received my Dell Inspiron (Rebranded IBM ThinkPad). Back then I made great use of it while going to school for programming and really appreciated not having to remove my hands from my keyboard just to move the cursor across the screen. Fifteen years later I don't do too much programming any more, but I've been using my Lenovo UltraNav at work for drafting release documentation and software specifications in Word as well as some technical artwork in Illustrator. My 'i' key has been shorting out so was really looking forward to replacing it with a Yoda.

My initial impressions after taking it out of the box were that this thing was HEAVY! Easily the compact keyboard is heavier than that old Dell Inspiron which was quite a beast in itself. I was already making plans to purchase a second one to use with a Surface, but there is no way I'd want to tote this brick around. Thankfully this one was destined for my office desk where the weight has no impact and I can appreciate the stability that the heavy frame provides. That said I'd really like to see a lighter model produced if I were to afford a second purchase for a mobile setup

I went for Cherry Clear switches for this board. While I've never used a board with them, I wanted give them a go after all the frenzy about them I've been seeing online. This is the second Cherry switch type board I've owned. Two previous boards were Cherry Black and I must say I really don't like the response from them. I'm a big gamer myself and am one of the oddballs that play Street Fighter on a keyboard. So much so that I show up to tournaments and play on console with a keyboard using adapters. I can tell you Cherry Black switches are not fast enough. While I can write a separate article about it, button up response time is just as important as button down response; it's because up always has priority over down and forward has priority over back. This is especially important when performing instant air moves where after pressing up to jump, you need to immediately press down to forward, or down to back in order to perform the move as close to the ground as possible. After spending Sunday playing on the board I can say with confidence that Cherry Clear switches are not fast enough either. While it's a pleasure to type this review on, and Cherry Clears are perfectly fine for typical PC Gaming, my HHKB 2 Lite board simply out performs the response of the switch (or any other switch I've used).

Although I'm pretty sure that most people are not buying this board with gaming in mind. It's bought because it's compact and functional; above all else it's bought for the trackpoint.

In its default state the trackpoint appears to be very sensitive and way too fast. In trackpoints I've used in the past I've had to turn down the mouse speed in windows while increasing the sensitivity in my mouse to get a nice balance. I've seen a few people say it's too sensitive themselves, perhaps I've gotten acclimated to it over the years, but I've been able to work with the default sensitivity. After all it's probably a good thing to make it more sensitive than preferred as it's simple to decrease the pressure resolution, but sloppy to increase it. Just keep in mind that you may want a mouse that can control its own sensitivity as no trackpoint that I know of has its own on board memory for these settings; including the Tex Yoda.

Another odd behavior that the Yoda maintains with the trackpoint which other trackpoints abide by is the middle mouse button. By default it behaves as a scroll button, and not a mouse 3 button. This means pressing the button by itself does not open links in a new window, or close tabs. Its scroll behavior is also not analogous to what you get when pressing mouse 3. Instead of displaying a scroll icon which effects scrolling how far away your cursor is from it, while holding the middle button your cursor does not move but the page will scroll dependent on how much force you are pushing the trackpoint up or down. For better or worse it does not scroll from side to side. Although I kind of wish it would, I can see how it may lead to sloppy behavior if it did. On the whole I've come to appreciate the scrolling method as I'm scrolling through pages and pages of documentation. Middle mouse functionality is not entirely missing. If you press left or right mouse buttons while holding the middle button you will get a middle click; however you also get left or right mouse clicks simultaneously as well. I've just been using the right mouse button as while you get a context menu while opening and closing tabs in the browser, it's manageable.

One final mention of the trackpoint; again as with all trackpoints the cursor will start to drift if held at precisely the same exact spot for a couple seconds. I've had this happen twice in the past week, but just not touching the trackpoint for a couple seconds will allow it to recalibrate where center is and resolve the issue.

The very first thing I did with my keyboard was install rubber O-rings on each of the keycaps. While Cherry clear switches are pretty quiet as is, the O-rings did provide a noticeable reduction in noise. Installing them however took marginally more work than expected. First, the board did not come with a keycap puller. This wasn't a big deal for me as I already had a really nice puller. I did also swap a few keys around at work which I pried off with my fingers. Wouldn't recommend it as you may break your stem, but I was lucky enough not to have that happen. The big issue however is that all of the larger keys have a rather unique stabilizer in them. The stabilizer is glued into the bottom of the keycap and clipped into the frame below. You can unclip the stabilizer to completely remove the key but on most I was able to hinge them just enough to slide the O-ring on and then press them back into the stem. I'd like to get custom keycaps for this board in the future, but I am concerned on replacing the larger keys as they are a rather custom fit.

As with all 60% keyboards, the location of the auxiliary functions is a custom job as well. For better or worse they do not mirror the HHKB layout, so for those of us who are accustomed to it, we need to learn a new layout for this board. It's a bit annoying, but let's be honest, the HHKB layout has some problems in its own design. While I'm use to using my right pinky for all the arrow keys, having them under IJKL is a much, much better location. What I am disappointed about however is the location of the home and end keys. When holding Fn+Shift to highlight an entire line your left hand needs to stretch to T and G respectively. Not a game breaker, but as I'm use to using my right hand to highlight text and code I feel U and O would have been much, much better locations for these.

I've also come to appreciate that Fn+Enter toggles the right shift button and accompanying modifier keys to arrow keys as well. This is a welcome addition as it makes adding markup or modifying line breaks and what not to several lines of text or code very easy. I've seen some complaints that it can be confusing when this accidentally gets switched on and the right hand Fn key cannot longer be used to turn it off, but still once I understood what was happening I've been able to make great use out of the functionality.

On the whole I've been very, very satisfied with my purchase over the past week. Beware of the weight, beware of the limitations of all other trackpoints, but other than that it's an impressive board!
